# PCRE2, prebuilt for Emscripten (wasm32)

Static build of PCRE2 10.44 targeting `wasm32-unknown-emscripten`, used only
by the wasm build so the `Regex` module (src/stdlib/regex.kex) works there
too. The native build is unaffected — it keeps finding PCRE2 via Homebrew or
the distro package.

No PCRE2 exists in Emscripten's port system, so this is built from source.
Use the same **Emscripten 5.0.7** the rest of the wasm build requires — see
`third_party/gmp-wasm/README.md`'s "Emscripten version" section for why that
pin exists. Building the library itself is not sensitive to the version, but
linking it into `kex.js` is, so there is no reason to keep two toolchains
around:

```
curl -LO https://github.com/PCRE2Project/pcre2/releases/download/pcre2-10.44/pcre2-10.44.tar.gz
tar xf pcre2-10.44.tar.gz
mkdir pcre2-10.44/build-wasm && cd pcre2-10.44/build-wasm
emconfigure ../configure \
  --host=wasm32-unknown-emscripten \
  --build="$(../config.guess)" \
  --disable-shared \
  --enable-static \
  --disable-pcre2-jit \
  --enable-unicode \
  --prefix=<repo>/third_party/pcre2-wasm \
  CFLAGS="-O2"
emmake make -j8
emmake make install
```

`--disable-pcre2-jit` is required: PCRE2's JIT emits native machine code for
the host architecture, which does not exist for wasm. The interpreted
matcher is used instead — slower per match than a JIT-compiled pattern, but
a browser REPL is not a regex benchmark, and correctness is what matters
here.

`--enable-unicode` backs `\p{...}`, `\w` under UTF, and the `PCRE2_UTF` /
`PCRE2_UCP` options that `src/interpreter/stdlib/regex.cxx` compiles patterns
with. Without it those patterns fail to compile at runtime rather than at
build time, so it is not optional.

`--build="$(../config.guess)"` matters for the same reason it does for GMP:
without an explicit build triple, configure can misdetect whether it is
really cross-compiling, because emcc-produced binaries run transparently
under Node on the build host.

Only `include/pcre2.h` and `lib/libpcre2-8.a` are actually linked (~430KB).
`make install` also drops `libpcre2-posix.a` and a `pkgconfig/` directory
here; both are unused and simply ignored. Nothing under this directory is
vendored — it is all build output, regenerated by the recipe above.
